clinicalPearls: Characterised by thickened, velvety palms with exaggerated dermatoglyphics giving a ridged, honeycomb appearance resembling the surface of bovine foregut (tripe).
Strongly paraneoplastic, with the great majority of reported cases occurring in association with an underlying malignancy.

The tumour association depends on coexisting acanthosis nigricans: tripe palms with acanthosis nigricans most often signals gastric carcinoma, whereas isolated tripe palms more often signals pulmonary carcinoma.
May be accompanied by the sign of Leser-Trelat and florid cutaneous papillomatosis as part of the same paraneoplastic spectrum.
Yellowish keratotic thickening of the palm with accentuated ridges over the finger pulps is typical.
Onset may precede diagnosis of the tumour and should trigger investigation for gastric and pulmonary primaries.
Skin changes may regress with treatment of the underlying malignancy and recur with relapse.
reference.pathophysiology: Tripe palms share the growth-factor-driven mechanism of malignant acanthosis nigricans, with which they frequently coexist. Tumour secretion of transforming growth factor alpha, acting through the epidermal growth factor receptor, together with fibroblast growth factor and insulin-like growth factor 1, stimulates keratinocyte and dermal fibroblast proliferation. The result is marked palmar epidermal hyperplasia with accentuation of the normal dermatoglyphic ridges, producing the characteristic rugose, velvety surface.
additionalDifferentials: Hyperkeratotic hand eczema or palmar psoriasis
additionalInvestigations: CT of the chest to identify lung carcinoma, especially with isolated disease
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with biopsy for gastric carcinoma when acanthosis nigricans coexists
CT of abdomen and pelvis for other primaries
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis, papillomatosis and acanthosis
Sputum cytology or bronchoscopy where a lung primary is suspected
Tumour markers directed by the suspected primary
redFlags: New tripe palms in an adult, particularly a smoker
Coexistent acanthosis nigricans or the sign of Leser-Trelat
Associated weight loss or systemic symptoms
reference.prognosis: Tripe palms indicate an underlying, frequently advanced gastric or pulmonary malignancy; prognosis is that of the associated tumour and is often poor.
pitfalls: Mistaking tripe palms for chronic eczema or occupational keratoderma
Not tailoring the tumour search to whether acanthosis nigricans coexists (gastric versus lung)
Missing an occult lung primary in a patient with isolated tripe palms
Failing to recognise recurrence as a sign of tumour relapse
